arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
transliteration: Lā yukallifu Allāhu nafsan illā wusʻahā
translation: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
notes: Reassurance that whatever difficulty a person is facing, Allah has already accounted for their capacity to bear it.

arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
transliteration: Fa-inna maʻa al-ʻusri yusrā, inna maʻa al-ʻusri yusrā
translation: So, verily, with hardship comes ease. Verily, with hardship comes ease.
notes: A repeated promise directly after describing difficulty, emphasizing that ease is not just possible but paired with hardship.
verification_note: Ayah 5 cross-checked against api.quran.com and corrected. Ayah 6 (identical wording minus the leading 'Fa-') was not independently fetched -- verify_corpus.py only spot-checks the first ayah in a range -- but is one of the most well-established repeated phrases in the Qur'an.

translation: Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
notes: Points to remembrance of Allah (dhikr) as a direct source of inner calm when the heart feels unsettled.

arabic: وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُۥٓ
transliteration: Wa man yatawakkal ʻalā Allāhi fahuwa ḥasbuh
translation: And whoever relies upon Allah - then He is sufficient for him.
notes: Directly addresses uncertainty about outcomes: reliance on Allah (tawakkul) is presented as sufficient, after one has done what is within their control.

translation: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
notes: Said by believers facing a threatening situation; a short, memorable affirmation of trust used widely for fear and anxiety.

arabic: وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يَا۟يْـَٔسُ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلْكَـٰفِرُونَ
transliteration: Wa lā tayʻasū min rawḥi Allāh, innahu lā yayʻasu min rawḥi Allāhi illā al-qawmu al-kāfirūn
translation: And do not despair of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people.
notes: Spoken in the story of Yusuf's family during prolonged hardship, as a direct command against giving up hope in Allah's relief.

arabic: قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا
transliteration: Qul yā ʻibādiya alladhīna asrafū ʻalā anfusihim lā taqnaṭū min raḥmati Allāhi inna Allāha yaghfiru al-dhunūba jamīʻā
translation: Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
notes: A direct address from Allah to those weighed down by sin, explicitly forbidding despair and affirming the scope of His mercy. (An earlier version of this entry had a single-letter transcription error turning 'forgives' into a nonsense word -- caught and fixed via scripts/verify_corpus.py.)

arabic: لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَـٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
transliteration: Lā ilāha illā anta, subḥānaka, innī kuntu min al-ẓālimīn
translation: There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.
notes: The dua of Prophet Yunus (Jonah) called out from extreme distress; widely recommended for anxiety and hardship combined with seeking forgiveness. (An earlier version of this entry had a single-letter transcription error turning 'wrongdoers' into a nonsense word -- caught and fixed via scripts/verify_corpus.py.)

arabic: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَـٰبَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
transliteration: Wa bashshir al-ṣābirīn, alladhīna idhā aṣābat-hum muṣībatun qālū innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʻūn
translation: And give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.'
notes: Frames patience through trials with a specific phrase to say at moments of loss, reorienting ownership of one's life back to Allah.
verification_note: The end of ayah 155 ('wa bashshir al-sabirin') was cross-checked against api.quran.com. Ayah 156 (the 'inna lillahi...' phrase) was not independently fetched -- verify_corpus.py only spot-checks the first ayah in a range -- but is one of the most universally known phrases in Islam.

arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
transliteration: Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa al-ḥayyu al-qayyūm, lā ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa lā nawm, lahu mā fī al-samāwāti wa mā fī al-ard, man dhā alladhī yashfaʻu ʻindahu illā bi-idhnih, yaʻlamu mā bayna aydīhim wa mā khalfahum, wa lā yuḥīṭūna bi-shayʼin min ʻilmihi illā bimā shā'a, wasiʻa kursiyyuhu al-samāwāti wa al-ard, wa lā ya'ūduhu ḥifẓuhumā, wa huwa al-ʻalīyyu al-ʻaẓīm
translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs all that is in the heavens and the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what will be after them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
notes: The single most widely memorized verse in the Qur'an, commonly recommended for protection and for calming fear or anxiety. Previously abbreviated with an ellipsis pending verification; now given in full, cross-checked against api.quran.com.

arabic: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآ ۖ إِنَّنِى مَعَكُمَآ أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
transliteration: Qāla lā takhāfā innanī maʻakumā asmaʻu wa arā
translation: He said, 'Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing.'
notes: Allah's reassurance to Musa and Harun before they faced Pharaoh -- a model for facing a frightening task while feeling accompanied and seen.

arabic: رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِىٓ أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَىَّ
transliteration: Rabbi awziʻnī an ashkura niʻmataka allatī anʻamta ʻalayya
translation: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me.
notes: The dua of Prophet Sulayman (Solomon) upon recognizing a blessing; a model for turning a moment of gratitude into a direct request for more of it.

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَىَّ وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
transliteration: Allāhumma anta rabbī, lā ilāha illā anta, khalaqtanī wa ana ʻabduka, wa ana ʻalā ʻahdika wa waʻdika ma istataʻt, aʻūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʻt, abūʼu laka biniʻmatika ʻalayya wa abūʼu laka bidhanbī, faghfir lī fa-innahu lā yaghfiru al-dhunūba illā anta
translation: O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no deity except You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I remain committed to my covenant and promise to You as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge to You Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge to You my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
notes: Known as 'Sayyid al-Istighfar' (the master formula of seeking forgiveness); the Prophet described whoever says it with certainty during the day or night and dies that same day or night as entering Paradise.

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ، وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
transliteration: Allāhumma innī aʻūdhu bika min al-hammi wal-ḥazan, wal-ʻajzi wal-kasal, wal-jubni wal-bukhl, wa ḍalaʻi al-dayni wa ghalabati al-rijāl
translation: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and stinginess, and from being overcome by debt and overpowered by people.
notes: A dua the Prophet taught for regular recitation, pairing anxiety and grief together with several other burdens people commonly carry.

arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلاَ أَقْدِرُ وَتَعْلَمُ وَلاَ أَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتَ عَلاَّمُ الْغُيُوبِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِي الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ
transliteration: Allāhumma innī astakhīruka bi-ʻilmika, wa astaqdiruka bi-qudratika, wa asʼaluka min faḍlika al-ʻaẓīm, fa-innaka taqdiru wa lā aqdir, wa taʻlamu wa lā aʻlam, wa anta ʻallāmu al-ghuyūb. Allāhumma in kunta taʻlamu anna hādhā al-amra khayrun lī fī dīnī wa maʻāshī wa ʻāqibati amrī, faqdurhu lī wa yassirhu lī thumma bārik lī fīhi. Wa in kunta taʻlamu anna hādhā al-amra sharrun lī fī dīnī wa maʻāshī wa ʻāqibati amrī, faṣrifhu ʻannī waṣrifnī ʻanhu, waqdur liya al-khayra ḥaythu kāna thumma arḍinī bih
translation: O Allah, I seek Your guidance by virtue of Your knowledge, and I seek ability by virtue of Your power, and I ask You of Your great bounty. You have power, and I have none. You know, and I do not know. You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know this matter to be good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me. And if You know this matter to be bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me, and turn me away from it, and decree for me what is good wherever it may be, and make me content with it. (He then names his specific need.)
notes: The Prophet taught this as a full structured dua (salat al-istikharah, preceded by two non-obligatory rak'ahs) for any matter of importance one is undecided about. An earlier version of this entry cited hadith 1162, which is actually an unrelated report about a different prayer -- the correct number, confirmed against the fawazahmed0/hadith-api dataset (sourced from Sunnah.com's own text), is 1166, and the dua is now given in full rather than abbreviated.

arabic: عَجَبًا لأَمْرِ الْمُؤْمِنِ إِنَّ أَمْرَهُ كُلَّهُ خَيْرٌ وَلَيْسَ ذَاكَ لأَحَدٍ إِلاَّ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ إِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ سَرَّاءُ شَكَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ ضَرَّاءُ صَبَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ
transliteration: ʻAjaban li-amri al-muʼmin, inna amrahu kullahu khayr, wa laysa dhāka li-aḥadin illā lil-muʼmin: in aṣābathu sarrāʼu shakara fa-kāna khayran lah, wa in aṣābathu ḍarrāʼu ṣabara fa-kāna khayran lah
translation: How wonderful is the affair of the believer; there is good for him in every matter, and that applies to no one but the believer. If something good happens to him, he is grateful, and that is good for him. And if something bad happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him.
notes: Describes both gratitude and patience as being 'good' for the believer regardless of the situation, reframing every outcome as an opportunity rather than only good outcomes. An earlier version of this entry cited 'Sahih Muslim 2999', a bare consecutive number that could not be confirmed and pointed to an unrelated hadith when checked against the fawazahmed0/hadith-api dataset; replaced with the unambiguous book/hadith-within-book reference from that same source, which does match narrator (Suhaib) and content exactly.

arabic: لَيْسَ الشَّدِيدُ بِالصُّرَعَةِ، إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ
transliteration: Laysa al-shadīdu bi-al-ṣuraʻa, innamā al-shadīdu alladhī yamliku nafsahu ʻinda al-ghaḍab
translation: The strong person is not the one who overcomes people through his strength, but the strong person is the one who controls himself when he is angry.
notes: Redefines strength as self-control in anger rather than dominance over others.

translation: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan. The Prophet said this to two men who were exchanging insults, one of whom had gone red-faced with rage, telling the onlookers this phrase would remove what he was feeling.
notes: A short phrase specifically prescribed as a practical response in the moment of anger, rather than only general advice about anger. An earlier version of this entry incorrectly appended 'al-rajim' (the accursed) to the phrase, conflating it with the separate formula recited before reading Qur'an -- this hadith's actual wording is shorter, confirmed against the fawazahmed0/hadith-api dataset (sourced from Sunnah.com's own text).
